name: Gedor
overview: Gedor is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Mered and his Jewish wife. This detail situates him within the lineage of Judah, emphasizing his tribal heritage and family background as recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:18. No additional notes expand on his character or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Gedor appears as a proper name in Scripture without an accompanying meaning or divine attribution. It is simply presented as a personal name in the biblical text of 1 Chronicles 4:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Gedor as the son of Mered and his Jewish wife, and he is also inferred to be the father of Jered. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Gedor's significance lies in his placement within the genealogical record of Judah, which underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant people and the continuity of the Messianic line through the tribe of Judah. While the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal achievements, his mention affirms the importance of family lineage in God's redemptive plan. His inclusion in 1 Chronicles highlights the historical and tribal identity that frames the story of God's people.
